Find the parametric equations of the hyperbola shown above given that its asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}x.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
x=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,
$$

where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants.

The vertices of the hyperbola occur at $(0,\pm a).$ From the graph, we have that $(0,-3)$ is a vertex of the hyperbola, so $a=3.$

Recall also that the asymptotes of the hyperbola occur at $y=\pm \frac{a}{b}x.$ In our case, the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}}x.
$$

Equating the coefficients of $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{a}{b} & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{3}{b} & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \\ b & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the hyperbola are

$$
x=\sqrt{5}\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$
